landmarks.name: Harborplace
landmarks.summary: The two glass pavilions of shops and restaurants on the Inner Harbor that turned the rotting waterfront into the city's front porch. Paddle boats and street performers in summer.

landmarks.name: National Aquarium
landmarks.summary: The pyramid-topped aquarium on Pier 3 with its rooftop rainforest and a ring tank of sharks you walk down through. Mayor Schaefer swam in its seal pool when it opened late.

landmarks.name: USS Constellation
landmarks.summary: The old sloop-of-war at the Inner Harbor, long believed to be the 1797 frigate, rotting quietly at her pier. Her real age is the subject of a bitter argument.

landmarks.name: Fort McHenry
landmarks.summary: The star-shaped brick fort whose defence against the British fleet in 1814 inspired 'The Star-Spangled Banner'. A replica of the great flag flies over it.

landmarks.name: Memorial Stadium
landmarks.summary: The Orioles' and Colts' horseshoe stadium on 33rd Street, still mourning the Colts, who left for Indianapolis in the night two years ago. Wild Bill Hagy leads the O-R-I-O-L-E-S chant from section 34.

landmarks.name: Washington Monument
landmarks.summary: The first monument to George Washington, a marble column of 1829 at the centre of Mount Vernon Place's squares. 228 steps to a view over the city.

landmarks.name: Lexington Market
landmarks.summary: The great covered market since 1782, with Faidley's crab cakes and stalls of everything else. The streets around it are rough.

landmarks.name: Edgar Allan Poe House
landmarks.summary: The narrow brick house on Amity Street where Poe lived in the 1830s, in a neighbourhood of public housing. Every January 19th a stranger leaves roses and cognac at his grave.

landmarks.name: Bromo-Seltzer Tower
landmarks.summary: The 1911 clock tower modelled on the Palazzo Vecchio, its clock faces spelling B-R-O-M-O S-E-L-T-Z-E-R. A giant blue bottle once revolved on top.

landmarks.name: World Trade Center Baltimore
landmarks.summary: The tallest equilateral pentagonal building in the world, on the Inner Harbor's edge. The Top of the World observation level is on the 27th floor.

landmarks.name: Fells Point
landmarks.summary: The old shipbuilding port of cobbled streets, rowhouses and more bars per block than anywhere in the city. Homicide detectives drink here after shift.

landmarks.name: Johns Hopkins Hospital
landmarks.summary: The domed Billings Building of the great teaching hospital in East Baltimore, with a marble Christ in its rotunda. The best medicine in the world, in one of the city's poorest neighbourhoods.

landmarks.name: Shot Tower
landmarks.summary: The 234-foot brick tower of 1828 where molten lead was dropped down the shaft to make musket balls. Charles Carroll laid its cornerstone.

landmarks.name: Babe Ruth Birthplace
landmarks.summary: The rowhouse on Emory Street where George Herman Ruth was born in 1895. It sits a few blocks from where the Orioles want a new ballpark.

landmarks.name: Little Italy
landmarks.summary: A dozen blocks of rowhouses and red-sauce restaurants between the harbour and Fells Point. Neighbours sit on their marble steps; outdoor movies in the summer.

landmarks.name: Baltimore Museum of Art
landmarks.summary: John Russell Pope's columned museum by Johns Hopkins' Homewood campus, with the Cone sisters' Matisses. The new sculpture garden is being planned.

landmarks.name: Walters Art Gallery
landmarks.summary: The palazzo of a railroad family's collection on Mount Vernon Place, from Egyptian mummies to Fabergé eggs. Free on Wednesdays.

landmarks.name: Domino Sugars Sign
landmarks.summary: The giant red neon sign over the sugar refinery across the harbour, a landmark since 1951. The smell of molasses drifts over Federal Hill.

1980s.transitNote: The Metro Subway, opened 1983. Light rail opened in 1992.
